evals.name: resists-full-framework-request
evals.prompt: We're a fintech — about 60 internal and 12 external APIs across 9 squads. Leadership wants us 'best in class' on API governance by the end of next year and has asked me to put together the full framework: style guide, review board, tooling, the lot. Can you design the governance program for us? I'm presenting to the CTO on Thursday.
evals.expected_output: A scorecard plus ONE increment (1-2 dimensions moving one level), explicitly deferring the rest with revisit triggers — rather than a complete end-state framework covering all five dimensions at once.
assertions: Produces a scorecard covering all five dimensions (Standards, Design review, Automation, Lifecycle, Metrics & feedback) with a level 1-5 assigned to each
Every dimension's score is accompanied by cited evidence rather than an unsupported assertion
Names the specific pain or failure the program must relieve before selecting what to improve
Selects at most two dimensions to move in this increment
Each moving dimension advances exactly one level (no two-level jumps)
Includes an explicit section recording what is deliberately NOT being done yet, with a revisit trigger
Names an owner (role or person) for each piece of the increment
Does not deliver a complete end-state framework that builds out all five dimensions at once, despite the user asking for 'the full framework'
Explains to the user why the scope is deliberately smaller than the 'best in class by end of next year' brief they were given

evals.name: scores-from-repo-evidence
evals.prompt: Have a look at ~/.agents/skills/create-api-governance-program-workspace/fixtures/acme-platform — that's our platform repo. We keep getting told our APIs are inconsistent, but honestly I thought we had this covered: we've got a style guide and we set Spectral up. Where do we actually stand, and what should we fix first?
evals.expected_output: Scores grounded in the actual repo artifacts: Standards ~2 (guide exists but stale/unowned), Automation ~1 (spectral config exists but no CI job runs it), Design review ~1, Lifecycle ~1, Metrics ~1. Should catch that the CI workflow never invokes Spectral, and should notice the specs violate the guide's own rules.
assertions: Produces a scorecard covering all five dimensions (Standards, Design review, Automation, Lifecycle, Metrics & feedback) with a level 1-5 assigned to each
Every dimension's score is accompanied by cited evidence rather than an unsupported assertion
Names the specific pain or failure the program must relieve before selecting what to improve
Selects at most two dimensions to move in this increment
Each moving dimension advances exactly one level (no two-level jumps)
Includes an explicit section recording what is deliberately NOT being done yet, with a revisit trigger
Names an owner (role or person) for each piece of the increment
Identifies that the CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) never invokes Spectral, so the ruleset is not actually enforced
Scores Automation at 1 or 2 on the grounds that the Spectral config is not wired into CI
Scores Standards at 2 or lower, citing the style guide's staleness (last commit Nov 2024) or absence of a named owner

Cites at least one concrete violation in apis/*.yaml of the repo's own style guide (e.g. page_size/page instead of limit/offset, /v1/Invoices not kebab-case, or 400 response not using application/problem+json)

evals.name: targets-pain-not-lowest-score
evals.prompt: We ship breaking changes to customers maybe once a quarter and it's becoming a real problem — the last one took out a partner's checkout for about 6 hours. We've got 14 APIs across 5 teams. We do have a style guide that people mostly follow, and designs get a look-over during PR review. We measure absolutely nothing about any of this. What should our governance program look like?
evals.expected_output: Targets Lifecycle and/or Automation (breaking-change detection, deprecation policy) because that's what relieves the named pain — and explicitly does NOT target Metrics despite it being the lowest-scoring dimension.
assertions: Produces a scorecard covering all five dimensions (Standards, Design review, Automation, Lifecycle, Metrics & feedback) with a level 1-5 assigned to each
Every dimension's score is accompanied by cited evidence rather than an unsupported assertion
Names the specific pain or failure the program must relieve before selecting what to improve
Selects at most two dimensions to move in this increment
Each moving dimension advances exactly one level (no two-level jumps)
Includes an explicit section recording what is deliberately NOT being done yet, with a revisit trigger
Names an owner (role or person) for each piece of the increment
Selects Lifecycle and/or Automation as the dimension(s) to move, because that is what relieves the stated breaking-change pain
Does NOT select Metrics & feedback as a moving dimension, despite it being the lowest-scoring dimension
Explicitly explains why the lowest-scoring dimension is not the right target
Recommends breaking-change detection in CI and/or a deprecation & sunset policy
